description: The ONLY IPC granted to the remote Verse page (http://127.0.0.1:7777, the local sidecar's own origin, which the CSP already pins). Three window-chrome commands plus the native folder chooser, and nothing else: dragging the window by its top strip, double-click-to-zoom on that strip, emitting the `shell-theme` event so the native window background can match the UI and dark mode does not flash white on the next launch, and `dialog:allow-open` so 'Open folder…' can show a real directory picker instead of making the operator type an absolute path. THIS FILE, NOT main.json, IS WHERE A VERSE PERMISSION GOES: the Verse page is a remote origin, and a capability without a `remote` block never reaches it — the grant would look right in review and be rejected at runtime with no visible error. Deliberately excluded: every shell:* permission (an XSS in the console must not become command execution), the updater, the filesystem, and app show/hide. `dialog:allow-open` is the narrowest of the dialog permissions — it only shows a chooser the user must confirm and returns the chosen path; it reads no file contents, and `dialog:allow-save`, `dialog:allow-message`, `dialog:allow-ask` and `dialog:allow-confirm` stay ungranted, so page code cannot forge a native prompt. Do not widen this list further — put new native behaviour behind a window event evaluated from Rust instead (see shell_contract.rs).
